Retrieved December 22, 2008. The European edition was released on June 1, 2009. ==History== The album is a collection of some of Springsteen's hit singles and popular album tracks through the years. Springsteen released a similar ''[[Greatest Hits (Bruce Springsteen album)|Greatest Hits]]'' album in 1995. Unlike the previous release, this album is billed to "Bruce Springsteen & [[The E Street Band]]", the first time Springsteen's backing band has been credited with a compilation release. As such, it contains no Springsteen material recorded between 1984 and 2002, during which period he did virtually no studio recording with the E Street Band.[https://web.archive.org/web/20081223220416/http://www.rollingstone.com/rockdaily/index.php/2008/12/22/bruce-springsteen-plans-wal-mart-only-greatest-hits/ "Bruce Springsteen Plans Wal-Mart Only 'Greatest Hits{{'"}}], ''[[Rolling Stone]]'', December 22, 2008. Springsteen's association with [[Walmart|Wal-Mart]] drew puzzled reactions from the media, given the singer's longtime support for labor causes and the [[Criticism of Wal-Mart#Employee and labor relations|company's longtime anti-union actions]].{{cite news | url=http://bostonherald.com/entertainment/music/general/view.bg?&articleid=1144901 | title=Non-union label: Bruce Springsteen silent on his Wal-Mart exclusive | author=Gottlieb, Jed | work=[[Boston Herald]] | date=2009-01-13 | access-date=2009-01-16}} ''[[Huffington Post]]'' writer Tony Sachs pronounced the release one of the "top five boneheaded music industry moves of 2008",{{cite news | url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/tony-sachs/the-top-five-boneheaded-m_b_155010.html | title=The Top Five Boneheaded Music Industry Moves Of 2008 | author=Sachs, Tony | work=[[The Huffington Post]] | date=2009-01-03 | access-date=2009-01-16}} while ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' wrote that it reflected the duality of "the liberal singer-songwriter and the commercial juggernaut recording artist." Longtime Springsteen writer [[Charles R. Cross]] said that fans were now more accepting of such blatant commercial strategies given the overall slump in the music business. Nevertheless, the release did draw criticism from some fans as well as from labor union activists and independent record store owners.{{cite news | url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB123204420598786423 | title=Born to Run – and Promote | author=Smith, Ethan | work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] | date=2009-01-16 | access-date=2009-01-16}} In response, Springsteen manager [[Jon Landau]] said, "[L]et's start with the premise that Bruce is already in Wal-Mart. Wal-Mart has been 15% of our sales in recent years. It's not a question of going into Wal-Mart; we're there. They, and other retailers, are all looking for some way to differentiate themselves, and we try to accommodate each one. We're not doing any advertising for Wal-Mart. We haven't endorsed Wal-Mart or anybody else."{{cite magazine | url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/269553/bruce-springsteen-prepping-darkness-reissue | title=Bruce Springsteen Prepping 'Darkness' Reissue | author=Waddell, Ray | magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] | date=2009-01-23 | access-date=2009-01-23}} But then Springsteen himself, during publicity for his appearance at [[Super Bowl XLIII]], admitted that they "dropped the ball" with the association with Wal-Mart, and attributed it to insufficient vetting due to too many activities going on.{{cite news | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/02/01/arts/music/01pare.html | title=The Rock Laureate | author=Pareles, Jon | author-link=Jon Pareles | work=[[The New York Times]] | date=2009-02-01 | access-date=2009-01-29}} ==Track listing== All songs written by Bruce Springsteen except where noted. ===US edition=== # "[[Rosalita (Come Out Tonight)]]" – 7:00 #* From the album ''[[The Wild, the Innocent & the E Street Shuffle]]'', 1973 # "[[Born to Run (song)|Born to Run]]" – 4:29 #* From the album ''[[Born to Run]]'', 1975 # "[[Thunder Road (song)|Thunder Road]]" – 4:48 #* From the album ''Born to Run'' # "[[Darkness on the Edge of Town (song)|Darkness on the Edge of Town]]" – 4:32 #* From the album ''[[Darkness on the Edge of Town]]'', 1978 # "[[Badlands (Bruce Springsteen song)|Badlands]]" – 4:02 #* From the album ''Darkness on the Edge of Town'' # "[[Hungry Heart]]" – 3:19 #* From the album ''[[The River (Bruce Springsteen album)|The River]]'', 1980 # "[[Glory Days (Bruce Springsteen song)|Glory Days]]" – 4:19 #* From the album ''[[Born in the U.S.A.]]'', 1984 # "[[Dancing in the Dark (Bruce Springsteen song)|Dancing in the Dark]]" – 3:59 #* From the album ''Born in the U.S.A.'' # "[[Born in the U.S.A.
